topics.topic: Gate and completion evidence for post-restore reconciliation
questions: What prevents service access from being enabled before the required post-restore privacy reconciliation is complete?
What prevents service access before the required post-restore reconciliation has actually been completed?
What prevents service tokens from being enabled before the required reconciliation is complete, and what evidence marks completion?

quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question and text as P9, which found that owner-only startup and the owner's host procedure are the specified gate and evidence.

precedent.topic: Verifiable gate completing reconciliation before service access resumes
quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done.
precedent.why: The texts deliberately assign quarantine and reconciliation enforcement to the owner's host procedure and explicitly state that Registry cannot verify completion.

topics.topic: Mechanism preventing restoration from reopening the one-time import
questions: How is restoration of a pre-import backup prevented or detected so that the one-time import cannot reopen?
Is the migration closure's permanence only an operational promise by the owner, or must Registry be able to detect and refuse a restored pre-import store?
How is restoration of a pre-import backup prevented or detected?
What mechanism, if any, makes the claim that a pre-import backup is never restored true?

quotes:
The owner never
restores a backup made before the import, which its recorded instant
shows, so the import stays closed (A16 rule 10, R0-79).

Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions): the owner decrypts it
   with the key it was made with, kept in the vault (rule 3).

The owner never
   restores a backup made before the import, which its recorded instant
   shows, so the import stays closed (A16 rule 10, R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts any structurally valid restored store and can therefore reopen import after a pre-import restore; another keeps independent import-completion evidence and refuses such a store. The owner and subsequent import callers notice whether a second import becomes possible.
judgement.why: The rule asserts that the owner never performs the restore but leaves Registry's behavior after that forbidden restore unverifiable and unspecified.

topics.topic: Whether audit sequence monotonicity and uniqueness survive restoration
questions: Does sequence-number uniqueness cover the store's full pre-restore history, or only the restored lineage now present?
May a restore reuse sequence numbers that were written after the restored backup, or must monotonicity survive restoration?
May post-restore entries reuse sequence numbers that production wrote after the restored backup, or must a high-water mark survive outside the restored store?

quotes:
Sequence numbers are never reused in a store (M09): changes that write an
   entry are applied one at a time, and each entry takes the number after the
   last its store ever wrote, kept in the store apart from the entries, so an
   erasure does not lower it.

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it, and numbering continues from the backup's
   last number (A15); the lost entries exist nowhere.
judgement.why: Continuing from the backup's last number reuses numbers written after that backup, contrary to the rule that a store never reuses a number and advances after the last it ever wrote.

topics.topic: Detection and cleanup of incomplete or plaintext backup temporary files
questions: How does Registry identify and handle incomplete backup and decrypted temporary files left by a process or host failure?
What happens if removal of the plaintext temporary file fails?

quotes:
Right after writing a backup Registry checks it: it decrypts it into a
   temporary file in the backup location, opens it for reading only, checks
   that it is the store version of its release, that the store's own
   integrity check passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded
   sequence number, and removes the temporary file.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation fails startup or backup processing and securely removes or quarantines leftover encrypted and plaintext temporary files; another continues serving while leaving or ignoring them. The owner and anyone able to inspect the backup location notice the files and the possible plaintext exposure.
judgement.why: The texts require removal and no partial file but define no behavior for a crash or a failed removal of the decrypted temporary file.

topics.topic: Disposal of other sessions' uploaded import files after import acceptance
questions: When any session accepts the one import, are uploaded files in all other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?
When one session accepts the import, are uploaded files in other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?

quotes:
An accepted import drops the
   file of the session that confirmed it; a file another session keeps stays
   until that session ends, and its confirmation is refused because the
   import is closed (rule 8).
judgement.why: A16 expressly retains other sessions' files until those sessions end and drops only the confirming session's file.

topics.topic: Filesystem states that permit creation of a new store
questions: Exactly which filesystem states authorize Registry to create a new store, and which must fail startup?
Exactly which configured store-location state causes Registry to create a new store, and which states fail startup?

quotes:
A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no
   default to any item.

An empty store location is
   made into a new, empty store of the running release's version at the start;
   otherwise the store must open for reading and writing and carry the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats only a nonexistent configured path as an empty location and refuses empty files or directories; another initializes an existing zero-length file or empty directory. The owner notices whether startup creates a fresh store or fails, with materially different risk of overwriting an intended store.
judgement.why: The startup rule does not define which filesystem state constitutes an empty store location.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and scope
questions: Which exact cookie attributes and scope enforce the stated browser boundary, particularly because cookies are not scoped by port?
What exact Secure, SameSite, Domain and Path policy applies, especially when Registry is reached locally without HTTPS?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question as P12 about cookie attributes, scope and local HTTP behavior.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and deployment rules, including local HTTP support
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Response to request-id collisions with records outside the granted project set
questions: What happens when Kernel supplies an allowed project and a request id already carried by a room or pointer of a different project outside its session's set?
What does Kernel receive if its room or pointer request id collides with a record belonging to a project outside its granted set?

quotes:
A create whose request id an existing record carries, with facts that
   differ from that record's current ones — a different value, or the record
   corrected since — is refused, and nothing changes; the caller reads the
   record.

For 'add a room' and
   'publish an artifact pointer' the project is one of the facts.

Every refusal of the third check, and of a project that does not exist, is
   the same answer as for a project that does not exist (R0-47); a call naming
   an unregistered session is answered as a call outside the set (R0-53).

Registry does not depend on Kernel's own check (R0-46), and no refusal tells
   the agent that a project exists.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns or exposes the collided room or pointer as A01's instruction that the caller reads the record suggests; another hides the collision behind the not-found answer because the existing record belongs to an ungranted project. Kernel and the agent notice whether data or existence outside the granted set is disclosed.
judgement.why: A01 does not say whether authorization is rechecked against the existing record's project when its globally unique request id collides with a call naming another allowed project.

topics.topic: Rules for retaining or replacing imported project display names
questions: When must confirmation require a replacement display name instead of accepting the v1 name, and how can Registry determine that the v1 name identifies a person?
When may the v1 display name be retained, and how is the required renaming of a person-named project enforced or confirmed?

quotes:
Projects imported
under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import.

When the owner picks the projects to import, the owner may give each a new
display name and an alias (R0-82); the project arrives under them, its id kept.
judgement.why: R0-82 requires person-named imported projects to be renamed, while R0-85 and A16 make a replacement optional and otherwise retain the v1 name.

topics.topic: Treatment of backups and entries newer than the restored snapshot
questions: Are post-backup entries required to be destroyed from every newer backup during restoration, or does “exist nowhere” mean only that they are absent from the restored live store?
What happens to backups newer than the snapshot selected for restoration?

quotes:
Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it, and numbering continues from the backup's
   last number (A15); the lost entries exist nowhere.

Every day at the same run — whether the new backup succeeded or not —
   Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before.
judgement.why: Entries newer than the restored snapshot can still exist in retained newer backups for up to 30 days, contrary to the statement that they exist nowhere.

topics.topic: Validation of malformed or conflicting records in unselected projects
questions: Must malformed records and conflicts belonging solely to unpicked projects be detected and shown?
Do malformed records and conflicting ids belonging only to unpicked projects appear in the mapping or affect the import?

quotes:
Registry checks what the picks bring in — each picked project with the
   rooms and pointers that name it and the v1 value it names — and nothing
   else of the file; a room or pointer naming another project belongs to that
   project: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked,
   shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id
   check.
judgement.why: Rule 3 explicitly says records belonging only to unpicked projects are not checked, shown as conflicts or imported.

topics.topic: Whether a new owner sign-in invalidates existing owner sessions
questions: What happens to the owner's existing sessions when the owner signs in again?
May several owner sessions coexist, or does a successful sign-in invalidate an earlier one?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.

The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable).
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits several independently valid owner sessions after repeated sign-ins; another invalidates all earlier sessions on each successful sign-in. The owner notices whether older browsers and their pending confirmations or uploaded import files remain usable.
judgement.why: The texts create and end individual sessions but do not state the effect of a successful sign-in on existing sessions.

topics.topic: Whether in-flight owner requests survive sign-out or restart
questions: May a request that passed the session check commit after a concurrent sign-out?
Does an in-flight owner request that already passed session validation complete if the session is signed out or the instance begins restarting before it commits?

quotes:
The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable).

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit passes while it runs.
judgement.divergence: One implementation lets a request that passed validation commit after concurrent sign-out or during a graceful restart; another cancels or rechecks it and refuses the commit. The owner and every consumer of the changed record notice whether the action takes effect.
judgement.why: The completion rule covers expiry limits but does not say whether sign-out or restart invalidates an already admitted request.

topics.topic: Which retained backup may be restored under the recovery-point guarantee
questions: Must restoration use the newest successfully checked backup, or may the owner choose an older retained backup and lose more than a day?
Which retained backup may the owner restore if the at-most-one-day loss guarantee is to hold?

quotes:
While the daily runs succeed, an erasure reaches the backups at most 30
   days after it, and a restore loses at most a day of changes; a failed run
   lengthens both by the days until a run succeeds.

Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions): the owner decrypts it
   with the key it was made with, kept in the vault (rule 3).

Every day at the same run — whether the new backup succeeded or not —
   Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before.
judgement.divergence: One recovery procedure requires the newest successfully checked backup and loses at most one day during successful daily runs; another permits any retained backup and can lose up to 30 days. The owner, services and callers notice the different restored records and lost changes.
judgement.why: The recovery-point guarantee does not specify which retained backup the owner must select to satisfy it.
